discovery: Prediction and discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, founding moiré quantum matter

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics (2D materials, strongly correlated electrons)
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted in 2011 that at a 'magic' twist angle near 1.1 degrees, the moiré pattern in bilayer graphene produces flat electronic bands. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group built precisely controlled tear-and-stack devices and found correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity there, confirming the prediction. This work turned the twist angle into a new control parameter for quantum matter. The resulting field of moiré materials has since produced orbital ferromagnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect, Wigner crystals, and fractional Chern insulators without magnetic field, in graphene and transition-metal dichalcogenide superlattices. These systems are tunable in situ by gate voltage and are now studied in laboratories across the world, including in India. Few discoveries of the past two decades have changed so much of how experimental condensed-matter physicists design and probe correlated electron systems.
